headline: Oncology models borrow from external cohorts, references and cell lines to generalise
label: Cross Domain Transfer In Oncology
summary: New preprints borrow from cell lines, older cohorts, methylation atlases or other cancers to strengthen tumour classification and survival prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is importing structure learned elsewhere into data-limited oncology prediction tasks. MODAE+ uses multi-objective deep domain adaptation to move cell-line pharmacogenomic drug response onto TCGA tumours. A layer-specific transfer elastic net borrows from older breast cancer cohorts for multi-omics survival prediction in patients under 50. An axillary lymph node deep-learning model is tested for metastasis prediction in other cancers. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomic features with external methylation atlases to improve lung cancer early detection. DeSCENT adds reference-informed cellular profiles derived from bulk RNA-seq to TCGA survival models. Related work constrains or audits models rather than transferring them. CAISL anchors LUAD survival models on clinical variables with sparse molecular correction. OncoSpot simulates Visium-like data with known subclones and CNAs to benchmark CNA inference. A 1.3M-slide study maps how much sex, age and race is recoverable from H&E foundation-model features, which bears on confounding in transferred representations.
